papers.title: Jhāna Dalam Buddhisme
papers.abstract: Jhāna merupakan salah satu konsep sentral dalam praktik meditasi Buddhis yang berkaitan dengan perkembangan konsentrasi mendalam (samādhi). Dalam tradisi Buddhisme Theravāda, jhāna dipahami sebagai kondisi absorpsi mental yang dicapai melalui pengembangan samatha-bhāvanā. Meskipun demikian, pemahaman tentang jhāna sering menjadi bahan diskusi dan perdebatan dalam kajian Buddhisme modern, khususnya mengenai perannya dalam pencapaian Nibbāna, potensi bahaya dalam praktiknya, serta perbedaan interpretasi antara sumber kanonik seperti sutta dan komentar klasik seperti Visuddhimagga. Artikel ini bertujuan menjelaskan pengertian jhāna, karakteristiknya, hubungannya dengan realisasi spiritual, serta kontroversi yang muncul dalam studi Buddhisme kontemporer. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah studi literatur terhadap sumber-sumber kanonik Buddhis, komentar tradisional, dan penelitian akademik modern. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa jhāna memiliki posisi penting dalam jalan menuju pembebasan, tetapi interpretasi mengenai fungsinya dalam praktik meditasi masih menjadi diskusi terbuka di kalangan sarjana dan praktisi Buddhisme.

papers.title: Generative AI in Human-AI Collaboration: Validation of the Collaborative AI Literacy and Collaborative AI Metacognition Scales for Effective Use
papers.abstract: Abstract Advancements in AI’s conversational capabilities and situational awareness mean that now, humans work with AI collaboratively. However, these developments affect the skills needed to use AI effectively. In this study, we address the need to update measures of AI-related knowledge and skills to reflect the collaborative capability of advanced AI tools by developing and validating two new scales focusing on collaboration and metacognition. A survey of 292 users of collaborative AI tools was conducted. Both the Collaborative AI Literacy and Collaborative AI Metacognition scales showed good internal consistency and predictive validity. Structural equation modeling supported their convergent and discriminant validity. Both measures correlated with users’ assessments of the benefits from working with collaborative AI tools. As predicted, Collaborative AI Metacognition explained significant variance beyond that explained by general Metacognition. These validated scales provide an important resource for assessing and researching knowledge and skills for working with Collaborative AI tools.

papers.title: How creative self-efficacy influences problem-solving skills in engineering education: the dual mediating role of critical thinking and metacognition
papers.abstract: Problem-solving skills are a core competency for engineering students, yet the psychological mechanisms underlying their development remain poorly understood. Creative self-efficacy has been identified as a potential motivational driver of problem-solving skills, but the pathways through which it functions have received limited empirical investigation. This study examines the direct relationship between creative self-efficacy and problem-solving skills and explores the dual mediating roles of critical thinking and metacognition in this relationship. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with a sample of undergraduate engineering students (N = 711). Validated self-report scales were used to assess creative self-efficacy, critical thinking, metacognition, and problem-solving skills. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was employed to test the proposed dual mediation model. Creative self-efficacy was found to have a statistically significant direct effect on problem-solving skills (p < 0.01), although the effect size was weak (f² = 0.031). In contrast, creative self-efficacy had strong effects on both critical thinking (p < 0.001, f² = 0.690) and metacognition (p < 0.001, f² = 0.676). Both critical thinking (p < 0.01) and metacognition (p < 0.001) significantly mediated the relationship between creative self-efficacy and problem-solving skills, though their direct effects on problem-solving were modest (f² = 0.035 and f² = 0.129, respectively). The findings demonstrate that creative self-efficacy primarily enhances problem-solving skills through its positive effects on critical thinking and metacognition. These results highlight the need for engineering education to strengthen students’ critical thinking and metacognition while fostering their confidence in their problem-solving. These insights offer both theoretical and practical guidance for designing targeted interventions to enhance students’ problem-solving skills.

papers.title: Metacognition meets AI: Empowering reflective writing with large language models
papers.abstract:
Reflective writing is known as a useful method in learning sciences to improve the metacognitive skills of students. However, students struggle to structure their reflections properly, limiting the possible learning gains. Previous works in educational technologies literature have explored the paradigms of learning from worked and modelling examples, but (a) their application to the domain of reflective writing is rare, (b) such methods might not scale properly to large‐scale classrooms, and (c) they do not necessarily take the learning needs of each student into account. In this work, we suggest two approaches of integrating AI‐enabled support in digital systems designed around learning from worked and modelling examples paradigms, to provide personalized learning and feedback to students using large language models (LLMs). We evaluate Reflectium, our reflective writing assistant, show benefits of integrating AI support into the learning from examples modalities and compare the perception of the users and their interaction behaviour when using each version of our tool. Our work sheds light on the applicability of generative LLMs to different types of providing support using the learning from examples paradigm, in the domain of reflective writing.
What is already known about this topic

Reflective writing fosters metacognitive skills and improves learning gains and personal growth.
The learning from worked and modelling examples paradigms is effective for skill acquisition and applying the acquired knowledge.
Existing reflective writing assistants usually lack dynamic, AI‐driven feedback or interactivity, limiting personalization and adaptability to each user's own needs in the learning process.
What this paper adds

It introduces Reflectium, an AI‐enabled reflective writing assistant, integrating intelligent and interactive writing support for both the learning from worked and modelling examples paradigms.
It demonstrates the use of a fine‐tuned large language model (LLM) for providing feedback in the learning from worked examples version, and an LLM‐powered conversational agent simulating instructor interactions for the learning from modelling examples version.
It reports findings from a user study comparing the positive impact of artificial intelligence (AI) support on learners' performance, interaction behaviour and learning experience.
Implications for practice and/or policy

Digital tutoring systems for teaching reflective writing using the learning from worked examples paradigm should incorporate adaptive AI feedback to enhance learning gains.
Conversational agents simulating peers/instructors and powered by LLMs can provide scalable, interactive support for learning from modelling examples, notably in large‐scale educational settings.
Reflective writing tools should be evaluated for their impact on different aspects of the learning process, such as task performance, interaction behaviour and user experience, to guide future improvements.
Educators and policymakers should consider the integration of AI‐driven reflective writing tools into teaching curricula to enhance reflective practices and metacognitive skill development.

papers.title: Knowing (Not) to Know: Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Human Metacognition
papers.abstract: Many organizations seek to combine human expertise with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), but they often overlook a core requirement for effective collaboration; humans must understand their own abilities. This understanding of one’s own abilities is referred to as metacognition, which captures how well individuals monitor and regulate their own decision making. In two experiments with real estate and lending professionals, we find that XAI improves human metacognition by reducing their overconfidence. As a result, experts can better delegate decisions to an artificial intelligence (AI) and interact with it more effectively, improving the collaborative performance. These effects occur primarily when XAI highlights differences between human reasoning and AI logic. Our findings demonstrate that metacognition is a key mechanism through which XAI affects decision outcomes and offer guidance for organizations deploying (X)AI under growing transparency and accountability mandates, such as those in the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act.

papers.title: The community of inquiry, shared metacognition, and student engagement in online learning: a systematic review
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Although the community of inquiry (CoI) is a crucial theoretical framework for understanding student performance, little is understood about how shared metacognition and student engagement play a part in online learning in higher education. The Covid-19 pandemic increased the importance of effective online learning. This study searched Web of Science Core Collection and EbscoHost (ERIC) databases for peer-reviewed literature (January 2015 - November 2022). This study used the PRISMA 2020 protocol. Twenty-one studies were analysed considering the CoI, shared metacognition and student engagement in online learning. The data was synthesised to understand the dynamics between the CoI presences, co- and self-regulation, and student engagement. The results indicated minimal studies on student self- and co-regulation, application, and observation behaviour. More research is required on learning presence and social regulation within the CoI. This study recommends further research on the impact of shared metacognition and student engagement in the CoI. For students to be successful in online learning, more research must be done on how students regulate and engage online to enhance a community of practice. The study adds value by examining empirical data in the literature investigating CoI, shared metacognition and student engagement in online learning for higher education settings.

papers.title: Changes in Dietary Behavior, Physical Activity, and Mental Health During a Lifestyle-Based Wellness Program for Women Re-Entering the Community After Incarceration: A Single-Arm Pre-Post Program Evaluation.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Women re-entering the community after incarceration experience substantial chronic disease and mental health burdens. Evidence regarding lifestyle medicine programming in transitional housing settings remains limited. This study evaluated changes in dietary behavior, physical activity, and mental health symptoms during a wellness program. METHODS: This single-arm, uncontrolled pre-post program evaluation retrospectively analyzed existing survey data from 17 women residing at a transitional living facility in Houston, Texas. The program included weekly yoga and meditation sessions and monthly nutrition and cooking classes. Dietary behavior was assessed using an adapted 10-item Healthy Eating Assessment, mental health symptoms using the PHQ-4, and physical activity using frequency items from the IPAQ Short Form. Larger controlled studies with validated measures and longer follow-up are needed.

papers.title: Reclaiming agency: how women build mood, confidence and social connections during perimenopause.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to understand women's lived experiences of perimenopause, with reference to brain fog, mood, confidence and social connectedness, and identify opportunities to promote well-being. METHOD: A qualitative, exploratory study was conducted using semi-structured interviews with 30 midlife women in Australia from culturally diverse backgrounds. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Participants described perimenopause as a recurring disruption-stabilization cycle rather than a linear decline. Destabilization was often triggered by sleep loss, cumulative life load and symptom variability, shaping appraisals of mood and confidence. Brain fog was experienced as cognitive disruption accompanied by fatigue and self-doubt, commonly worsened by stress, poor sleep and diet. Participants actively engineered stability using individualized, multi-component strategies, including pacing and withdrawal, sleep optimization, physical activity and well-being practices, organizational and compensatory tools, acceptance and reframing, dietary adjustments, leisure and cognitive stimulation, and social support. Social connectedness was recalibrated, with shifts in engagement, mixed experiences of support versus misunderstanding and a strong preference for validating spaces and relationships. CONCLUSION: Perimenopause was experienced as dynamic yet manageable through structured self-management and supportive contexts. Findings support holistic, multimodal care that integrates symptom management with sleep, behavioral, cognitive and social interventions.

papers.title: The effect of mindfulness-based counseling on shame in women with human papillomavirus.
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the impact of mindfulness-based counseling on shame in women with Human Papillomavirus (HPV), addressing the gap in standardized mental health support and the often-overlooked emotional distress in HPV care. This randomized controlled trial was conducted in 2024 at Ayatollah Mousavi Hospital in Zanjan, Iran. Participants were recruited during routine visits and randomly assigned to intervention or control groups (70 per group) using block randomization. The intervention group received standard care plus eight weekly 90-minute mindfulness-based group counseling sessions (one in-person, seven virtual). The control group received standard medical care and health education. External shame was measured using Goss et al.'s Questionnaire. papers.title: Competency Scale for Developmentally Supportive Parenting of High-Risk Infants (CS-DSPHI): Development and Psychometric Testing.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Developmentally supportive parenting (DSP) is the parental competency that optimizes developmental outcomes in high-risk infants, spanning developmental knowledge, emotional responsiveness, cognitive stimulation, and the psychological capacity to sustain these behaviors. Existing measures assess caregiving confidence or require trained observers; none captures DSP competency by self-report. PURPOSE: This study aimed to develop a self-report scale measuring DSP competency among parents of high-risk infants and to evaluate its psychometric properties. METHODS: A total of 440 parents of high-risk infants participated in the study between February 2 and 28, 2024. The study was conducted in 2 phases. In Phase 1, the instrument was developed through a review of the relevant literature and interviews with parents; thereafter, the preliminary items were evaluated for content validity. Phase 2 included psychometric testing, item analysis, and construct validity analysis. Concurrent validity, internal consistency, and test-retest reliabilities were also examined. RESULTS: The final scale was confirmed using exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, yielding a 4-factor scale with 28 items. The 4 factors were parental knowledge of child health and development; parental emotional support; cognitive development promotion and behavioral guidance; and parental mindfulness and self-care. Concurrent validity was demonstrated, and instrument reliability was deemed acceptable. IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE AND RESEARCH: The CS-DSPHI is a valid and reliable instrument for assessing DSP competency in parents of high-risk infants. Healthcare providers can use these scores to identify specific areas requiring educational support and guidance. Further validation across diverse parent populations and infant risk levels is warranted.
